qa.note: The code check found nothing: the six files hold their recorded bytes and nothing else changed. The 74 checks of the local checks, the scans and the privacy gate passed. The test check found 11 gaps in coverage, 3 not minor: no check reaches the scan wrapper's fail-closed branches (status 2); the allowlist table's negative controls exist only in the plan and scratch fixtures, with no committed repeatable check; and the two controls that must still be reported are never observed on the hosted Linux runner. The 8 minor ones: more ignore-list membership tests with an isolated user-level ignore file, an assertion that the clone holds no ignore file for findings, anchor fixtures for the table, a counts-only assertion over the scan output, assertions around the two reads of the hosted runs, optional shell-syntax checks of the workflow's run blocks, and one row of the test plan re-attributed. Every fix is in the plan's own procedure, so the plan is revised first and the revised checks then run.

All 202 checks passed, as in the build's own run, and the seven files hold the revised plan's recorded bytes; every finding of Quality Review 1 is answered. 15 findings (14 test, 1 code), 2 not minor. First, the code finding, in the controls script `.github/scripts/allowlist_controls.py`: its two fixtures meant to test the anchors of the table's pinned text put the extra character inside the quotes, which the pinned pattern includes, so both stay reported even if an anchor is dropped: a later edit removing an anchor would leave the controls green (found by evaluating the patterns, not by a run with the binary). Second, on the hosted runs the log's counts-only property is read through four marker counts only, so a line of another shape in a scan step would go unnoticed in a log that becomes public with the repository. The 13 minor ones: the controls script's own failure paths and three more table mutations as repeatable steps; three sub-cases of the scan wrapper; assertions on the workflow's timeout, names and concurrency group; a parse check of the two scripts; standard error asserted empty; the workflow's failing shell branches run locally; more not-ignored paths for five root-anchored patterns; a direct check of the pure functions; and wording in the plan (a count of 95 commits that should read 94, seven lines that should read six, two rows of the test plan table, some check labels). The plan is revised first, then the revised checks run.

The code check found nothing: the seven files hold the plan's recorded bytes, and the code finding of Quality Review 2 is answered: evaluated against the rule and the table themselves, the committed table fails none of the controls' eleven expectations, and each of the four de-anchorings of the pinned text fails exactly its own fixture in both modes. All 334 checks passed (local checks 130, scans 199, privacy gate 5), and 13 of Quality Review 2's 15 findings are answered in full. 7 findings remain, all minor test findings, each an edit to the plan's procedure or its wording and none to the seven files: one call at the end of the canary step leaves its standard error unasserted; in two places the verdict is asserted before the shape check; one case is filed under the component row of the test levels though it runs git; three failing-side cases lack a shape and standard-error value; the 22 control lines and the controls each mutation turns are asserted as counts only, and reading the document from the last commit has no case; three more uncaught exits of the scan wrapper have no case; and the generated word's form and two helpers have no check of their own. They touch the checks before the landing, the allowlist controls, and the scan wrapper with its workflow. They are fixed on the spot and the steps they touch run again; no further review follows.

rows.title: Phase 0 · 5 — Make KotlinBottools public with secret scanning and push protection

qa.note: The repository is in the intended state and the issue's three criteria are met: it reads public with secret scanning and push protection enabled, every pre-rewrite id probed answers as absent, the feeds list none, and all nineteen issue bodies equal the intended text. Nothing was run again: the recorded results read 171 passed, 0 failed and 224 without a stored result (155 self-test checks, 50 stage lines printed and not kept, 19 checks of the landing not yet due), as re-running the self-tests would remove the run's working sets. 17 findings (15 minor, 2 other; 12 test, 5 code). The 2 not minor: the totals of the six self-tests were never stored, and the second feed read came about three and a half minutes after the first where at least six were required, which the as-built record does not yet state. The 15 minor ones: the stale entry on the revisions count, a one-second error in the pre-flip gate's time and gap, no stored trace that the tools were checked after they were saved a second time (they equal their pins now), the wording on stage markers, and how the test plan files and records its checks. They touch the anonymous measurements, the third privacy gate and the pre-flip gate. The plan's wording is corrected first, then the as-built record.

Fifteen of Quality Review 1's seventeen findings are closed, the two that were not minor among them: the totals of five self-tests are kept (137 checks passed, 0 failed; the 18 stand-in cases of the anonymous helpers were not run again, a known gap), and the spacing of the feed reads is corrected in the plan, stated in the as-built record and answered by the third feed read. The issue's three criteria are met on fresh reads: the repository reads public with secret scanning and push protection enabled, all 87 pre-rewrite commits answer as absent, and nine feed reads list no pre-rewrite id. The closed record is untouched and the saved tools equal their pins. Nothing was run again in this pass: its test results are read from the run's kept results. 12 findings (12 minor; 9 test, 3 code), all wording: the anonymous REST budget still stated as about 45 calls in the consequences, the plan's summaries of the landing's reads naming three of its five steps, one requirement number cited for the revert trigger, test plan rows that claim slightly more than their checks reach, and three statements of the as-built record (the measurements of the issue-text stage, the refusals that left no stored reply, one time stamp that straddles a second). They touch the anonymous measurements and are fixed on the spot, with no further review.

Both rewrites are confirmed by an independent recount: every expected value holds on both fresh mirrors, both remotes show only the one branch moved, and each acceptance criterion is met by evidence read from the log, the records and the remotes. The tools' two self-tests passed again in isolation (191 checks: 59 and 132). 23 findings (17 minor, 6 other; 19 test, 4 code). For the as-built record: one departure from the output rule not yet listed (a passing self-test prints a traceback with a sandbox path) and three small differences between the plan's wording and the tools. Follow-ups for the next rewrite unit: the classifier's reading of a reply's form, a close-out step that is not safe to run twice, and an anonymous budget reading that is not explained. Test gaps in the tools, the main ones: no case with a reply in its real shape, none for the stop that keeps a push from being sent twice, none for the closing controls of a probe set, the output rule asserted for one step only, and one self-test script that cannot be run by test level. They touch the push, the residual probes, the tools handed on and the check of the inputs. The landing's four document checks are still to run. How the findings on the tools are handled is not settled yet.

The rewrite, both pushes and every acceptance criterion stand, all nine recorded departures hold, and nothing outside the stated writes changed; `gdocs.sh` ran again with 22 passed. 12 findings (12 minor; 8 test, 4 code), every one small and on the records: three statements in the consequences that do not hold against the tools (when the classifier's gap lets a request be sent again, which probe stop a self-test case reaches, and the budget thresholds), a list of untested paths that is not complete, one departure not yet listed in the as-built record (each push request sent as a reference to its file with a checksum, asking for the one-shell run), and the document checks, which ran before the boards were last regenerated and run again before the documents are committed. They touch the push, the residual probes and the tools handed on. This review counts 20 test findings in Quality Review 1, where that pass's record holds 19.

rows.title: Phase 0 · 7.1 — Extend the workspace tools for BotTools, TrumpBot and Support

qa.note: The run was green: all 637 checks passed (gating 49, deterministic 63, component 80, integration 420, nonfunctional 23, and 2 of the coverage check), with the tool folder proved equal to its pins first; a green run does not clear what the review found. 32 findings (18 minor, 14 other; 22 test, 10 code). Tests: four cases of the clone set run uncounted in a subshell (424 case lines against a total of 420); six stops of the push procedure, the private-repository probe selection and two arms of the push check have no case; the output-rule cases and the coverage figure prove less than the test plan says (278 distinct texts for 308 sites; 8 stop sites of the Python tools outside it). Tools: a failed read of the webhook count and a failed read of the pull-request refs pass as zero or empty; the rename retry can move the old clone inside the target; a failed web fetch prints a local path; the resend decision reads a stale class; a missing record compares equal; the carried folder’s name is matched as a pattern. Plan text: the class table against the flowchart, and a stop the documents tool does not hold. They touch the self-test, the clone set, the rewrite set, the residual set, the parameter table, the tool folder, the recorded gaps and the readiness reads. The fixes change the tools’ source held in the plan, so the plan is revised first, then the folder is saved again and the steps run again.

The run was green: all 744 checks passed (gating 68, deterministic 63, component 80, integration 504, nonfunctional 22, and 7 of the coverage check), every total as the plan records and no console line that is not a case, note or runner line; a green run does not clear what the review found. 18 findings (16 minor, 2 other; 15 test, 3 code). Of Quality Review 1's 32 findings, 28 are closed in the tools with their cases, and the landing's documents are left to the landing; three test findings stay open in one part each, all minor now. What stands: one site where the coverage check proves less than it says (a stop text shared by a helper and one arm of the clone tool is reached by one line); a wait line that prints the year 1970 as the reset time when the server sends no reset header; the Python tools' own tests writing to the system's temporary folder; two fault fixtures whose address the stand-in does not redirect; the console case missing output at its start and end; result lines and plain exits with no asserting case; labels that name a step and not a behaviour; and statements of the plan not carried through the moves of cases between test sets. They touch the self-test, the clone set, the rewrite set, the residual set, the tool folder and the recorded gaps. The tools change again, so the plan is revised first, then the folder is saved and every step run once more.

The run was green: all 833 checks passed (gating 79, deterministic 63, component 91, integration 565, nonfunctional 28, and 7 of the coverage check), every total as the plan records, no stray console line and no label printed twice; a green run does not clear what the review found. 22 findings (20 minor, 2 other; 14 test, 8 code). Of Quality Review 2's 18 findings, 16 are closed. One defect of substance stands, found twice, in the self-test: the stamp a test set writes reads the run's id in a way that prints the shell's own missing-file line, with a local path, when the gating checks never ran in that scratch folder, and the set still ends with status 0; the later units run their quick check that way. The rest are small: in the self-test, a region comment that files two groups of cases under the wrong set, four lines and stops with no asserting case and five labels that name a step or state the opposite of their rule; in the tool folder, a file a staged rename moves into the documents folder not counted as outside it; in the rewrite set, the per-ref verification's baseline check run after the deliveries are written, and two error streams still open; in the clone set, one error stream and two statements of the plan; in the residual set, a convention that waits for a time a wait line may not print; in the readiness reads, three changed reads and one checksum write with no case. They touch the self-test, the tool folder, the rewrite set, the residual set, the clone set and the readiness reads. Next: every finding fixed, the folder saved and every step run again, then one more review limited to what changed.

This review was limited to the 15 tool files changed since Quality Review 3, and the five kinds were not run again: their totals (853 checks, none failed: gating 84, deterministic 63, component 92, integration 579, nonfunctional 28, and 7 of the coverage check), every last line as recorded, no stray console line and no label printed twice, were verified from the records the last run left, and only the coverage check was run, once (7 checks, 393 of 393 sites reached). 4 findings (4 minor; 3 test, 1 code). Every finding of Quality Review 3 is closed, the quick-check defect included: a kind run where no run was started now prints case lines only, and a case asserts it. The four left are all in the plan's wording, none in a tool: in the rewrite set, a sentence said the post-run step discards a message it does not, and now says the step checks its two records first; in the self-test, two limits were not stated (no case provokes the messages the post-run step discards behind checks that stop first; no fixture path holds a pattern character, so no case tells the residual close-out's literal strip from a pattern match), and two rounded run times were behind the recorded ones. They touch the self-test, the rewrite set and the residual set. All four were reworded in the plan, fixed in place with no additional review: no pin moved and nothing was run again.

rows.title: Phase 0 · 7.2 — Rewrite BotTools, TrumpBot and Support

qa.note: The run was confirmed independently from its stage markers, its log, its checksum lists and GitHub: 794 recorded checks, 789 passed and none failed, the other 5 not yet due (the landing's four document checks and the owner's reading of the as-built record); three histories rewritten, each pushed once and proven clean, every count at its expectation. 7 findings (7 minor; 7 test), none about what was pushed. Three typed checks (the earlier records, the earlier tool folder at its pins, the output rule over the unit's outputs) and the state read after the request service refused BotTools' first call leave no line in the run log, so the as-built record states their results; the plan's test table listed the grant read under two test sets and the input and record checks under none; the pin list's own checksum is to be stated at the start and at the close; and restoring the deny rule lifted for the push, with the allow lines removed, needs a follow-up. The procedure showed no defect: a first call refused is a case the plan provides for. They touch the outcome, the verification and the records, and in readiness the earlier records' check, the grant read and the pin list. The fixes are made in the documents: the plan's test table, the as-built record and the consequences.

rows.title: Phase 0 · 7.3 — Measure what GitHub still serves of BotTools, TrumpBot and Support

qa.note: The run was found correct and complete: every stage and step ran once with the planned lines and counts, the issue's four conditions are met, and nothing was written to GitHub. The eight findings are five wording points in the as-built record and the consequences: the count of runner steps (19, not 18), the anonymous budget's readings stated beside the calls made, the pace between probes, an acceptance section, and the outcome of the plan's assumptions. They touch the anonymous probes and the report rows.

items.title: Phase 0 — History rewrite: purge secrets and data from the six bot repositories
Phase 1 — Build skeleton: multi-module build, conventions, CI and repository scaffolding
Phase 2 — Core foundation: ids, failures, settings, storage ports and configuration
Phase 3 — Command model: definitions, validation, typed invocation, dispatch and help
Phase 4 — SQLite storage: migrations, erasure and backups
Phase 5 — Bot runtime: plugins, events, gateway, jobs, registration and built-in commands
Phase 6a — HTTP call surface: the bottools-http API, endpoint vocabulary, failures and test fake
Phase 6b — WebTools adapter: the internal adapter, composite build, strict pin, alignment checks and CI lanes
Phase 7 — Stats provider framework: provider SPI, account links, match tracker and game news
Phase 8 — Reaction-roles plugin, with the default role and welcome message on join
Phase 9 — Math plugin
Phase 10 — Admin plugin: typed get and set over guild settings
Phase 11 — Weather plugin: conditions and forecast from Open-Meteo
Phase 12 — Feeds plugin: RSS and Atom subscriptions with content safeguards
Phase 17 — Release 1.0.0 to Maven Central and archive the predecessor repositories
Phase 18 — Published test fixtures for plugin and provider authors (Experimental)
Phase 19 — Poker plugin: playable Texas hold 'em (Experimental)
Phase 23 — Desktop manager on SpartanUI and SpartanGraphics (unscheduled)
